messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I pushed a short RFC in the doc bucket: proposal to reduce the number of client-visible status variants. TL;DR: keep HTTP native (200/429/503/500) and add structured headers for routing/telemetry instead of inventing new surface codes.

Maria: 👍 can you paste the mapping here? worried the console and dashboards will lose meaning if we just collapse statuses.

Alex: Sure. Main idea — only expose these to clients: 200 (ok), 429 (rate/quota), 503 (service degraded/outage), 500 (internal). Everything else becomes internal-only and we attach metadata via headers and tracing.

Sam: How do we preserve fallback routing signals? we rely on distinct codes now to choose canary vs fallback pools.

Alex: routing will read X-RW-ROUTE-HINT + X-RW-FAILMODE in the response. SDKs can use those headers to decide local fallbacks. Not changing runtime routing decisions, just not surfacing new status codes to end users.

Sam: Example response headers?

Alex: ```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Content-Type: application/json
X-RW-ROUTE-HINT: region=us-east,variant=fallback
X-RW-FAILMODE: soft-degrade
X-RW-QUOTA-REMAINING: 12
```

Maria: That helps. Dashboard needs to show the internal breakdown though — can we add a telemetry dimension? e.g., event.status_internal = "cache_miss_fallback" and still surface the client-visible 503.

Jordan: Yes — telemetry will keep internal_status and route_hint tags. Console product tile will show both aggregated client impact (503/429 rates) and internal buckets. We should add a migration plan to the rollout: first emit headers + telemetry, then dark-launch SDK header parsing, then flip client surface.

Alex: Proposed rollout steps: 1) runtime emits headers + telemetry (no client change) 2) telemetry + console add internal bucket visualizations 3) SDKs add parser to expose friendly hints 4) flip to collapse extra statuses to 503/429 5) monitor regressions for 2 weeks and rollback if user-visible errors spike.

Maria: Agree but need clear gates: percent of requests with headers present, dashboard sampling completeness, and no increase in unexplained 5xxs.

Sam: One more ask — quota UX: if X-RW-QUOTA-REMAINING is low, SDK should emit a lightweight warning event, not fail. We don't want apps to panic.

Alex: Agreed. SDKs: warn at threshold 10, error only at 0. We'll add doc snippet.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for header-emission v1 to 5% traffic (eng-platform-canary).

Jordan: I'll add a console card mock with both "client-facing" and "internal" views. Posting link in #docs when done.

Maria: Thanks — feel better about this. small ask: keep a short changelog entry for support so they can map old codes to new ones.

Alex: will do. filing support mapping + migration checklist now. :white_check_mark:
